exclude: the unread twin of $E000-$EFFF: the routine at $5000 copies it there before the game starts, and the view's bitmap overwrites it once play draws
the unread twin of $F000-$FFFF: copied there by $5000, then overwritten by the second bitmap

comments.text: 6510 data direction register for the port at $01. The game never writes it: the one listed reference, STA $0000,X at $500B, is the hand-over copy loop whose operand high bytes $5011-$501A step up page by page, so that store really fills $F000-$FFFF.

6510 processor port, the memory banking. $8135 sets $36 while it sets up and $35 for play (RAM at $A000 and $E000, I/O at $D000); $80BA and $819E-$81BB set $36 around the KERNAL save/load; $B3BB sets $05 (cassette motor on) while CTRL+S/L waits for a key, $B3C8 puts $35 back. No write in the game sets $34 or $30, so the RAM under the I/O area is never visible to the game's code.

Pointer low byte ($02/$03), mostly a bitmap address: the row base from $55D0/$5540 plus $25 in the octant line routines $AC53-$ADCA and the dot plotter $ADCB, the row being filled by the horizon code $B0E1-$B196 and the unrolled fillers $BD00/$BE00, the star plots of $7319 and $AA95, the disc of $7508. $9575 uses it as the pointer to a building model (from $2600/$2700).

Pointer high byte, pair of $02: the bitmap page ($40-$5F or $60-$7F: row table $5540 plus $25 or $40); $AF6E starts it at $25 for the horizon fill, which steps it with INC/DEC; in $9575 the building model's page.

Low byte of the line-routine vector used by JMP ($0004) at $9D95: $9C1A loads it from $BC38 by the octant number in $67. The start-up disc routine $7508 uses $04/$05 as a bitmap pointer instead (the lower row, left half).
High byte of the line-routine vector (from $BC40 at $9C1F): with $04 it points at one of the eight octant routines $AC61-$ADAA. In $7508, the lower disc row's bitmap page.

Scratch byte shared by many routines: the product's low byte in $82BB and the first factor in $82D3, shift work in the float routines $8334/$838B/$84A7/$8510, Y save in the octant routines, the column in the key scan $B281, loop counter of the BCD money ops $8C73/$8C98 and of $8E88, row/column work in $871B/$8EC2/$950D, height bits in the building loader $9575, flag bits in $99DD and $9437.

Second scratch byte: the low byte of a 24-bit integer handed to $8510 (int to float) by $A5CE/$A61F/$9728/$94E0 and the starfields; the result sign in $82D3; the key being built by the matrix scan $B281 (row*8+column, bit 6 SHIFT, bit 7 CTRL) before it goes to $E9; reverse-video bit of the LOC figures ($B64C); saved Y in script op 21.

Float accumulator, mantissa byte (float: mantissa byte, then exponent byte = exponent*4 + sign in bit 0): operand and result of the log-table arithmetic $82FA (multiply), $8334 (divide), $838B (add), $828B (square), $8510 (int to float). Also a plain temporary: multiplicand of $82BB, argument of $8EC2 (view radius) and of $90BE (destination room, 0 = the surface), the octant routines' error term (starts at $80), the horizon's x fraction.

Float accumulator, exponent-and-sign byte, pair of $08: bits 7-2 the signed power of two, bit 0 the sign, bit 1 the carry catcher the add/multiply routines clear. Also a plain temporary: multiplier of $82BB, the $90BE entry offset into the room record, $886A's exponent offset for the missile speed, the horizon's integer x ($B0E1).

Float temporary 1, mantissa: partial sums in the view transform $A75C, the matrix build $A320, the clipper $99DD and $A4B2. Elsewhere a saved index: X in $871B, $8833 and $9602; the out-of-city flags shifted in by $8EC2; the first coordinate of the 2-D rotation $A728; a float in the disc routine $7508.
Float temporary 1, exponent byte (pair of $0A); also the saved Y of $8833 and the second coordinate of the 2-D rotation $A728.
Float temporary 2, mantissa (partial products in $A75C and $99DD); the product in $A728. In the start-up disc routine $7508 it is the upper row number, counting down from $43.
Float temporary 2, exponent byte (pair of $0C). In $7508 the lower disc row number, counting up from $44.
Low byte of a bitmap pointer used only by the start-up planet disc $7508: the upper row's right half ($02 + $A0).
High byte of the $7508 upper-row right-half pointer (pair of $0E).
Low byte of $7508's pointer to the lower row's right half ($04 + $A0).
High byte of $7508's lower-row right-half pointer (pair of $10). The next bytes, $12-$15, are not referenced by any code found.
Float temporary 3, mantissa: sin(roll)*sin(pitch), then cos(roll)*sin(pitch), in the matrix build $A320; in the horizon code $AF6E, tan(pitch) scaled by $21 (clamped to $00/$74 on overflow).
Float temporary 3, exponent byte (pair of $16). The BIT $17 at $FFBD is in RAM under the KERNAL that the tracer followed a JSR into, not game code.
Float add $838B: exponent byte of X,Y minus that of $08/$09; bit 0 then says whether the signs differ (add or subtract the mantissas). Read again at $8359 and $8410.

Loop index of the item being processed: the vertex number $A75C stores its results under (vertex loops $96D8, $9054, $9728, $A4B2), the edge number in $96E7 and $9054, the star number in the starfields $7319/$AA95, the map window width in $8EC2, the raster line of the wipe in $AE96/$AEF3.
Row counter: rows of the map window still to scan in $8EC2; in the horizon fill ($AF6E, $B0E1, $B178) the bitmap row being filled, from $78 up to $FF (136 rows through the tables $5558/$54C8).
Pointer to the current underground room's record, low byte, from $2300,X ($90FA); read by $90BE (entry position), $9162 (size, colours, name message, contents) and the door test $9437.
Room record pointer high byte, from $23C0,X (pair of $1B). $9127 writes back into the record through it: entering a transporter room rewrites that room's first door (record bytes 5 and 6).

Pointer to the current object's model, low byte, from $2800,X ($9728): byte 0 the last vertex number, then three bytes per vertex, each offset by $80 (read by $A61F), then the edge count and packed or byte-pair edges.
Object model pointer high byte, from $2840,X (pair of $1D).

Event-script program counter, low byte: the interpreter $8AB2 reads operations through ($1F),Y and the handlers step it ($8B92). Set from the word table $0800 ($7203, $8A8C); $7290 points it at $7001, the opening sequence's script.
Event-script program counter, high byte (pair of $1F); calls push both bytes on $BEC2 through $8BC9.

Projection scale as an exponent increment: $18, i.e. times 64 (the focal length in pixels), added to the exponent of X/Z and Y/Z before they become screen offsets ($A86B, $A91B, $AA3E) and used by the clipper $99DD and the horizon $B023. No code writes it; the value comes from the game's zero-page image ($BF21), which a saved position also restores. (The references from $FFC6/$FFC8 are RAM under the KERNAL, not code.)

Flight model turn rate (float, mantissa), in the vehicle handler $9F17: multiplied each pass by the damping $BEA2/$BEA3, joystick left or right adds $BEA4/$BEA5 or its negative; its integer adds to the heading $2C/$2D ($A102), and while airborne it sets the roll $28/$29 ($A119).
Flight model turn rate, exponent byte (pair of $22); $A11B adds $BEA7 to it to scale the bank angle.

Pass counter for the double buffer: $AF6E increments it each pass; bit 0 set means draw into $6000 and show $4000 ($25 = $60, $C7 = $70), clear the reverse. $90BE decrements it once when a door leads back to the surface. $FFC4 AND ($24,X) is RAM under the KERNAL, not game code.
High byte of the bitmap being drawn, $40 or $60, set by $AF6E each pass; added to the row table $5540 by the line routines, the dot plotter $ADCB and the horizon code.

Actual speed of the craft (float, mantissa): in $9F17 it moves towards the set speed $EC/$ED (times $BEAE/$BEAF, smoothed by $BEAA/$BEAB), then scales the step of the position. SPEED on the panel shows it ($B5A8, '+' or '-' from the sign) and its top bits set the engine note on SID voice 2 ($B5FC).

Actual speed, exponent byte (pair of $26); $9950 stores $88 (a value of about 2^-30, i.e. stopped). On the ground $A024 keeps the craft level, with no climb, until this exponent reaches $1C (a speed of 128 or more): the take-off speed.

Roll (bank) angle, low byte; the angle has 1024 steps per turn with the quarter in bits 0-1 of $29. Set while airborne from the turn rate ($A119), zeroed on landing ($A0B6) and by L ($98D5); $A544 takes its sine and cosine.
Roll angle high bits (pair of $28; only bits 0-1 count). The horizon code reads it to pick which side gets which fill ($AFDE, $B0B0).

Pitch angle, low byte (1024 steps per turn, quarter in $2B); $0200 is level, $0300 at start-up (the forward vector points straight down). Stick up/down adds or takes $BEA6 in flight ($9F60); on the ground below take-off speed $A02C holds it level. The EL dial follows it ($B67B).
Pitch angle quarter, 0-3 (pair of $2A): 2 = level, set by $80E8, $98DC and $A030; 3 at start-up ($7203); the interstellar ship's handler $AA62 sets 1 while $BEFE is 0 ($AA6E).

Heading, low byte (1024 steps per turn, quarter in $2D). Walking turns it by $AC per pass ($A1B2), flight by the turn rate ($A10C); boarding restores a vehicle's heading from $802A,X and L stores it back there. COMP shows it ($B809).
Heading quarter, 0-3 (pair of $2C, masked with AND #$03); 2 after start-up and CTRL+Q.
sin(roll) as a float, mantissa ($A544, from the table $5A00/$5B00 through $841F).
sin(roll), exponent byte (pair of $2E); read by $A320 and the horizon code $B035.
cos(roll) as a float, mantissa ($A544 through $841E, the sine a quarter turn on).
cos(roll), exponent byte (pair of $30).
sin(roll)/cos(roll) as a float, mantissa ($A544, divide $8334); the horizon code $AF6E uses it for the slope.
tan(roll), exponent byte (pair of $32).
cos(roll)/sin(roll) as a float, mantissa ($A544); $AFF7 turns it into the horizon's per-row step $7B/$7C.
cot(roll), exponent byte (pair of $34); its sign picks the horizon's direction $7D.

sin(pitch) as a float, mantissa ($A544): the height component of the forward vector, copied into the matrix as $4E/$4F; the flight model's climb rate ($A037) and the missile's vertical speed ($88B1) use it.
sin(pitch), exponent byte (pair of $36).
cos(pitch) as a float, mantissa ($A544); scales the horizontal step in flight ($9FB9, $9FE8) and several matrix entries.
cos(pitch), exponent byte (pair of $38).
sin(pitch)/cos(pitch) as a float, mantissa ($A544); the horizon code $B01E scales it by $21 into $16/$17.
tan(pitch), exponent byte (pair of $3A).
sin(heading) as a float, mantissa ($A544): the X step of walking ($A221) and flight ($9FF0), and the heading-only view transform $A979 used on foot and underground.
sin(heading), exponent byte (pair of $3C).
cos(heading) as a float, mantissa ($A544): the Y step of walking ($A1F6) and flight ($9FC1), and the transform $A979.
cos(heading), exponent byte (pair of $3E).

View matrix, screen-x row, weight of the X offset (float mantissa), built by $A320 from the roll, pitch and heading terms (sign flipped by $F1). $A75C: X' = dX*$40 + dH*$42 + dY*$44. Built on the surface in a craft, while falling or during the elevator ride; on foot and underground $A75C uses the heading alone ($A979).
View matrix screen-x row, X weight, exponent byte (pair of $40).
View matrix screen-x row, weight of the height offset (float mantissa): -sin(roll)*cos(pitch); $A37E also uses it to shift the view centre $8E.
View matrix screen-x row, height weight, exponent byte (pair of $42).
View matrix screen-x row, weight of the Y offset (float mantissa), from $A320.
View matrix screen-x row, Y weight, exponent byte (pair of $44).
View matrix screen-y row, weight of the X offset (float mantissa): $A75C forms Y' = dX*$46 + dH*$48 + dY*$4A.
View matrix screen-y row, X weight, exponent byte (pair of $46).
View matrix screen-y row, weight of the height offset (float mantissa): cos(roll)*cos(pitch); $A429 also uses it to shift the view centre $8F.
View matrix screen-y row, height weight, exponent byte (pair of $48).
View matrix screen-y row, weight of the Y offset (float mantissa), from $A320.
View matrix screen-y row, Y weight, exponent byte (pair of $4A).

View matrix depth row, weight of the X offset (float mantissa): cos(pitch)*sin(heading), the forward vector's X; $A75C forms Z = dX*$4C + dH*$4E + dY*$50, and a missile launched by $886A flies along ($4C, $36, $50).
View matrix depth row, X weight, exponent byte (pair of $4C).
View matrix depth row, weight of the height offset (float mantissa): a copy of sin(pitch) $36 ($A49A).
View matrix depth row, height weight, exponent byte (pair of $4E).
View matrix depth row, weight of the Y offset (float mantissa): cos(pitch)*cos(heading), the forward vector's Y.
View matrix depth row, Y weight, exponent byte (pair of $50).

Point being transformed, X (float mantissa): before $A75C the offset from the player along X, from $A5CE (scene vertex), $A61F (object vertex), $A67B (map corner) or $9728 (a whole object as one point); in the clipper $99DD endpoint A's view X' (from $0100); in the starfields the star's X.
Point being transformed, X, exponent byte (pair of $52).
Point being transformed, height (float mantissa); in $99DD endpoint A's view Y' (from $0180); in the starfields the star's Y; the start-up disc $7508 keeps a row value here.
Point being transformed, height, exponent byte (pair of $54).

Point being transformed, Y (float mantissa); in $99DD endpoint A's depth (from $0340); in the starfields the star's depth. The start-up approach $74CA uses $56/$57 as a 16-bit count from $03FF down to 0 while the planet grows, before $7203 starts the descent.
Point being transformed, Y, exponent byte (pair of $56); in $99DD endpoint A's depth exponent (from $0380).
Result of the view transform $A75C: X' (float mantissa), stored to $0100,Y; in $99DD endpoint B's X'.
View X', exponent byte (pair of $58), stored to $0140,Y.
Result of $A75C: Y' (float mantissa, the exponent raised by 1 at $A8ED for the pixel aspect), stored to $0180,Y; endpoint B's Y' in $99DD.
View Y', exponent byte (pair of $5A), stored to $02C0,Y.
Result of $A75C: depth Z (float mantissa), stored to $0340,Y; endpoint B's depth in $99DD.
View depth, exponent byte (pair of $5C), stored to $0380,Y; its sign bit becomes bit 7 of the clip code (behind the viewer).
X'/Z as a float, mantissa: the perspective x of the vertex $A75C is working on (stored to $0600,Y), endpoint A's in $99DD. The starfields keep the star's screen x here.
X'/Z, exponent byte (pair of $5E), stored to $03C0,Y.
Y'/Z as a float, mantissa, for the vertex in $A75C (stored to $7600,Y) and endpoint A in $99DD.
Y'/Z, exponent byte (pair of $60), stored to $0640,Y.
Endpoint B's X'/Z (float mantissa) in the edge clipper $99DD, loaded from $0600,Y.
Endpoint B's X'/Z, exponent byte (pair of $62), from $03C0,Y.
Endpoint B's Y'/Z (float mantissa) in $99DD, from $7600,Y.
Endpoint B's Y'/Z, exponent byte (pair of $64), from $0640,Y.
Slope of the line being drawn as a fraction 0-255 ($FF when the slope is 1), from $99DD; the octant routines $AC53-$ADCA add it to the error term $08 each step.

Line direction: $99DD builds bit 0 (sign of dy), bit 1 (sign of dx), bit 2 (steep), then $9C10 maps it through $BBD0 to the octant number 0-7 that picks the routine ($BC38/$BC40) and the edge-exit tables $BBD8/$BBE0.
Slope of the edge as a float, mantissa (dy/dx or dx/dy), from $99DD; used to move a clipped endpoint onto the screen edge.
Edge slope, exponent byte (pair of $68).
Screen x (0-159) of endpoint A: from $0680 or computed by $A75C, moved onto the edge by the clipper; the start x handed to the octant routine ($9D8D).
Screen y (0-135) of endpoint A (from $06C0 or $A75C, clipped), the start y of the line.
Screen x of endpoint B, where the octant routines stop (CPX $6C); replaced by the edge exit from $BBD8 when B is off screen.
Screen y of endpoint B, the octant routines' stop row (CPY $6D); replaced from $BBE0 when B is off screen.

Clip code of the vertex $A75C is projecting and of endpoint A in $99DD: bit 7 behind the viewer, bit 0 x off screen, bit 1 y off screen (stored to $0700,Y); the clipper widens it to edge bits 1 right, 2 bottom, 4 left, 8 top.
Clip code of endpoint B in $99DD (from $0700,Y); non-zero sends the line end to the screen edge.

Number of the scene's last vertex: $96D8 transforms vertices $70 down to 0. $950D copies the building's $89; the room builder $9162 starts at 7 (the box's eight corners) and counts it up as it adds each shape from the templates at $928A.
Number of the scene's last edge: $96E7 draws edges $71 down to 0 from $0580/$05C0. $950D copies the building's $8B; $9162 counts it up from 11 (the box's twelve edges).
Player X position, low byte of three ($74:$73:$72). Walking ($A22D) and flight ($A003) add to it; in a room $939E keeps $73:$72 between $00:20 and ($0440-1):DF.
Player X position, middle byte: the place within the grid square, $80 its centre; the elevator test wants $70-$73 ($B40C).
Player X position, high byte: the grid column shown by LOC (0-15 in the city, signed further out; $EF flags beyond +-99). 0 underground ($9162). Script op 6 tests it.
Player height, low byte of three ($77:$76:$75). $3F on the ground (landing, $A0BE; the ground vehicles' handler, $9F04); the elevator ride computes it from $CB ($A256).
Player height, middle byte; $8C/$8D and the altitude table $2A00 (view radius) are taken from it.

Player height, high byte: $7F at start-up (high above the city for the opening sequence), 0 on the ground; the Colony Craft pad is at $40xx ($A0E2). From $20 up, $9536 draws the fixed city outline from $902A instead of the map window.
Player Y position, low byte of three ($7A:$79:$78); room clamp as for X ($93BB).
Player Y position, middle byte (place within the square, $80 its centre).
Player Y position, high byte: the grid row shown by LOC (0-15 in the city, signed further out); 0 underground. Script op 6 tests it.
Horizon edge: fraction of the x step per bitmap row, from cot(roll) ($B018); $B13F/$B155 add or subtract it.
Horizon edge: whole pixels of the x step per row (pair of $7B).
Horizon direction flag, 0 or 1, the sign of cot(roll) ($B002): whether the edge moves right or left down the view, and which fill goes on which side. $7E is not referenced by any code found.

Landed flag: $3F when the craft or player is on the ground ($A0BC), 0 while airborne ($A0F9). L ($98CD), D ($9903) and E ($B408) need it set; while it is set the flight model does not bank ($A115) and holds the craft level below take-off speed ($A024).
Joystick directions from $DC00 bits 0-3, 0 = pressed (up, down, left, right), read by $B2FE; $A165 swaps left and right through $A17B while $F1 is set; walking and flight test it with BIT.
Joystick fire from $DC00 bit 4, 0 = pressed ($B2FE); $886A launches a missile when it reads 0.
Fill byte on one side of the horizon, $55 or $AA (colour from the screen matrix or from $A5), swapped with $83 when the view is upside down ($AFD5-$AFF5).
Fill byte on the other side of the horizon, $AA or $55 (pair of $82); the unrolled filler at $BD00 writes it.
$00 or $FF: EOR mask for the byte where the horizon crosses a row ($B125), set with $82/$83.
Grid column of the building now in the vertex arrays ($9568); $94FE rebuilds the scene when the player's $74 differs. $80 at start-up and CTRL+Q, which forces a rebuild.
Player height high byte when the scene was last built ($956E); no code found reads it.
Grid row of the building now loaded ($9572); compared with $7A by $9504.
Building model byte 0 (its last vertex number), written by $9575 beside $89; no code found reads this copy.
Last vertex number of the loaded building (model byte 0, $9589): $950D copies it to $70, the collapse step $96AC and the loader $95E5 count from it.
Building model byte 1 (its last edge number), written by $9575 beside $8B; no code found reads this copy.
Last edge number of the loaded building (model byte 1): the edge unpacking loop $95BA stops there and $950D copies it to $71.

Height term for the view centre (float mantissa): $94E0 sets the player's height middle byte divided by 16, or 16 when $77 is non-zero; $A320 multiplies it by $42 and $48 to offset $8E/$8F and the clip bounds.
Height term, exponent byte (pair of $8C); $90F6 stores $E0 (zero) on entering a room.
Screen x of the view centre: $50 (80) plus the height term times $42 ($A38E); added to every projected x ($A875, $AA48, $9CF7).
Screen y of the view centre: $44 (68) plus the height term times $48 ($A439); added to every projected y ($A925, $9CB2).
Left clip bound (float mantissa): -80 plus the height term ($A399); $9D0C uses it to put a line end on the left edge (x = 0).
Left clip bound, exponent byte (pair of $90).
Right clip bound (float mantissa, $A3A4); $9C82 puts a line end on the right edge (x = 159).
Right clip bound, exponent byte (pair of $92).
Top clip bound (float mantissa): -68 less the centre shift ($A444); $9D51 puts a line end on the top row.
Top clip bound, exponent byte (pair of $94).
Bottom clip bound (float mantissa, $A44F); $9CC7 puts a line end on row 135.
Bottom clip bound, exponent byte (pair of $96).
Edge number at which the building's lines change colour (model byte 2, $9597): $96E7 draws edges above it with the pattern set by $AE02 and the rest with $ADFC's. $9162 sets $FF in rooms.
Angle of the building's rotating part, low byte (1024 steps per turn): $A12B adds $A2 each pass unless the building is destroyed ($F2 bit 7).
Rotating part's angle, high byte (pair of $99); $A544 takes its sine and cosine into $9B-$9E.
Sine of the rotating part's angle (float mantissa), used by $A4B2.
Sine of the rotating part's angle, exponent byte (pair of $9B).
Cosine of the rotating part's angle (float mantissa), used by $A4B2.
Cosine of the rotating part's angle, exponent byte (pair of $9D).
Number of the building's vertices that rotate, from the low nibble of model byte 3 plus 1 (0 when that byte is 0): $A4B2 turns vertices 0 to $9F-1 about ($A0, $A1).
X middle byte of the rotation centre (model byte 4), added by $A4F8 to each rotated vertex.
Y middle byte of the rotation centre (model byte 5), added by $A537.
Rotation speed, the high nibble of model byte 3 halved (0-120 angle steps per pass), added to $99/$9A by $A12B.

Colour of %00 pixels in the view: the raster interrupt $B9BB writes it to $D021 at line 0. Set from $B27D (1, white), by the wipes ($AEA9, $AEF5), the elevator ride ($BAA1-$BB1F) and the flash $B244; $7259 fills $A3-$A7 from $B27D, $7293 $A3-$A6 from $72F6.
Written with the colour table but read by no code found (the screen matrix's %01 colour is the constant 6 in $BB48): $B27D gives 6, the starfield palette $AC31 other values.

Colour of %10 pixels: $BB48 puts it in the screen matrix's low nibble (with 6 above it) through $BB4F. The area colour $C4 after a wipe; $AFB8 cycles it through $BB7E while $F0 counts (transporter flash). $A7, next door, gets the byte $A9 from the 5-byte copy at $7259 and is never read.

Colour of %11 pixels, written into colour RAM by $BB4F (skipped when $D800 and $5C00 already match); from $C5 after a wipe, set with $A3 by the flash $B244 (0 after a crash, $11 when shot down). $80BA writes it plus 1 into $D800 to force the refill.

Scene mode: 0 on the surface, 1 inside a complex (set at the bottom of the elevator ride, $A2F1; cleared going up, $A298, or by a door to the surface, $90C2). The main loop $8562 picks its branch by it.

What the player is in: 0-7 the vehicle object of that number (B, $98A0), $80 on foot (L, $98E2), 9 falling ($8988 ship shot down, $A1E1 walking off the Colony Craft pad, $90CB door to the surface), $0A the opening descent ($7244); $80E8 sets 1. $9D99 loads that entry's 16 bytes of handler and flight constants into $BEA0; script op 34 tests it.
Walking step (float mantissa), $40 from $7203, never changed: $A1ED multiplies it by the heading's sine and cosine.
Walking step, exponent byte, $18 (pair of $AA; with $40 that is 80 position units, $0050, per pass); $A1ED XORs the direction (1 forward, 0 back) into its sign bit.
Heading change per pass while walking with the stick left or right ($A1B5), $10 (1/64 of a turn) from $7203 and $80E8.
Saved index: the byte offset into the object model in $9728/$A61F, into the room record in $9162, the missile's object slot in $886A.
Room walls hit this pass: $939E starts it at 0 and decrements it for each axis it clamps; copied to $F8.
Number of the object $9728 is handling (from the visible list $2980); read by the take/board test $97FA, $98B1 and the per-object rotation $A6AD.
Last vertex number of the current object's model (its byte 0), the end of $9728's vertex loop.
Set to 2 after a door takes the player to another room ($8587); each walking step ($A247) counts it down, and $8575 tests no door until it is 0.
Number of objects in the current room or on the surface ($CD): $9374 lists them at $2981 onwards; $9706 draws and tests them, $9425 searches them.
Loop counter of $9706 over the visible objects, from $B2 down to 1.
Highest object number $9374 scans, $3F from $7203 (objects 0-63).
Lowest used entry of the map-corner table $7540-$757F (it fills downwards from $3B, $3C-$3F being the current square's own lines); these share the vertex slots $B5-$3F with the scene ($9073).
Highest used entry of the map line tables $7580/$75C0 (entries 3 upwards, built by $8FC3); $9086 draws them.

The grid square the player is in as an index, row*16 + column ($951D), 0 outside the city ($8F1E), so no building is loaded for index 0 ($952D). Indexes the city tables $2600/$2700/$2B00/$2C00-$2F00; script op 31 and the missile hit test ($87A4) compare with it.
The new key for this pass copied by $9706 for the object test $97FA: T ($16) takes, B ($1C) boards; $FF once one object has used it.

Message printer: index of the current token in the message ($8E22), read through the operand $8E27 that $8DAA or script op 1 points at the message. Zeroed when a message starts.
Message printer: index of the next character within the current word or literal (read through the operand $8E0A); 0 means fetch the next token.
Message window frame counter: $8DC3 counts it every frame, scrolling one character per frame while it is below 26, then holding until it reaches $E1. The intro script pokes 100; $B3D6 waits for 30.
Frames a part of a message stays in the window before the next scrolls in ($8DD0): 8 in the zero-page image, poked by the scripts to $7D, $32, $19 and $96.
Frame counter, 0-49: the panel interrupt counts it and carries into the seconds at 50 ($BA60); the wipes wait on it.
Seconds clock, low byte (with $E4), counted by the panel interrupt; script op 7 tests it (reading until it is stable), op 2 zeroes it.
Seconds clock, high byte (pair of $E3).
Script call stack pointer: index into $BEC2 for the return addresses pushed by $8BC9 and pulled by $8BD2; 0 from $7203.

Message printer state: 0 idle, $FF while the text prints ($8DC0, $8C45), 1 when the text has ended and blanks scroll in ($8E52); counted down per part by $8DD6. The panel interrupt calls $8DC3 while it is non-zero, and the script interpreter waits.
The script operation byte being run ($8ABB): bits 0-5 pick the handler, bit 7 inverts a test and bit 6 makes a taken branch a call ($8B8C, $8B9E).
Random generator, low byte of the 16-bit shift register $F3:$E8: $ADEF shifts it right one bit with feedback from its own bits. Script op 10 compares its operand with it.

Newest key from the matrix scan (key number with bit 6 SHIFT and bit 7 CTRL), written by $B281 only when it differs from $EA; $B4B2 writes 4 once a key has been used. The dispatch $B331, the object test $9706 and script op 11 read it.
Key seen by the last scan, $FF when none is held ($B2F8): lets $B281 report a key only once, and the + and - speed keys repeat while held ($B356).
Number of objects carried, 0-10; their numbers are at $BEB1 upwards (T adds at $982D and refuses the eleventh, D drops the last one, $98FE). CTRL+Q scatters them ($85F2).
Speed set with the keys (float mantissa): a digit sets 0 ($B491), + and - multiply by 1.03 or 0.98 ($B499); the flight model $9F17 steers $26/$27 towards it.
Set speed, exponent byte (pair of $EC): from the digit's entry in $BC50 with SHIFT as the sign ($B48D); $88 (stopped) from $9950.
City map window state for $8EC2: 0 while the lines hold the whole 16 x 16 city (so it is not rebuilt), $FF for a partial window (rebuilt each time); $80BA sets $FF, $8FF8 $40.
Non-zero when LOC's X or Y is beyond +-99 ($B654); $9054 then draws no ground lines.
Transporter flash: $0A on entering a transporter room ($913F), $1F for the mirror room ($9371); $AF6E counts it down, cycling $A5 through $BB7E; doors are ignored meanwhile ($9437).
Mirror flag, 0 or 1, toggled by room $7F ($9353): XORed into the view's x signs ($A360, $AA13) so east and west swap, and $A165 swaps the stick's left and right.

Status byte of the current grid square, from $2B00 ($9580): bit 7 destroyed (the missile sets it at $8765; the spin stops, $9685 flattens the building), bits 5-6 read by $B53D for the panel colour when object $1A is carried.
Random generator, high byte (pair of $E8), rotated by $ADEF.

Grid index (row*16 + column) of the square whose building the missile hit ($875B).

The $2B00 status of the square before the missile hit ($8761), compared at $87C1. While the KERNAL's zero page is swapped in for a save or load ($819E-$8255) this address is the copy pointer's low byte.
Next character for the message window, stored at $5F8E by $8DEB (its value also sets the tick's pitch); $A0 is a blank. In the save/load code, the KERNAL-side copy pointer's high byte.

In the game's own zero page, $60: the low byte of $2160, the restart address that $8215 jumps through as $BFFD after a save or load ($B8F6 has swapped the page to $BF02-$BFFF). No game code writes it. In the KERNAL context of $819E it is the segment and SAVE pointer.
High byte ($21) of the restart address $2160 (pair of $FD); $FF beside it holds $7D and is not referenced by any code found.

Vertex table, 64 entries (one per vertex 0-63): view-space X' mantissa, float with its exponent at $0140; written by the transform $A75C (from $58), read by the edge drawer $99DD. The starfields $7319 and $AA95 keep each star's X here. It lies in the stack page: $0100-$01BF hold three of these tables, and the stack, reset to $01FF by $80C5 and $B3F1, keeps to $01C0-$01FF. CMP $0100 at $8ADF and STA $0100 at $8D1C are script ops 24/25, whose operands the script rewrites first.
Vertex table: view-space X' exponent byte, one per vertex (pair of the mantissas at $0100), from $59; the starfields' star X exponent.
Vertex table: view-space Y' mantissa, one per vertex, from $5A; its exponents are at $02C0 (not $01C0, which the stack uses). The starfields' star Y.
The KERNAL's PAL flag (1 PAL, 0 NTSC), read once by the hand-over at $5024, which loops back to $5000 for ever on NTSC. $02A7-$02BF are not referenced by any code found.
Vertex table: view-space Y' exponent byte, one per vertex (pair of the mantissas at $0180), from $5B; the starfields' star Y exponent.
Vertex table: depth Z mantissa, one per vertex (exponents at $0380), from $5C; the starfields' star depth, to which each frame adds the speed at $74C3 or $AC4E.

Vertex table: depth Z exponent byte, one per vertex (pair of $0340); the sign bit marks a vertex behind the viewer and $99EB compares two of these to choose which end to clip. The starfields set every entry to 1 (negative) before the first frame ($72FE, $AA7F), so each star is placed anew.
Vertex table: exponent byte of X'/Z, one per vertex (the mantissas are at $0600), from $5F by $A943; reloaded by the clipper $99DD.

Vertex table: world X low byte, one per vertex (24-bit with the middle bytes at $0440 and high bytes at $0740): 0 for building vertices ($9649), a template byte for room shapes ($9256), turned by the rotation $A4B2; $A5CE subtracts the player's X. The starfields keep each star's previous screen x here, to erase it.

Vertex table: world X middle byte of vertex 0 (the array runs on at $0441, $0444 and $0445, where the room builder writes single corners). For a room, corner 0 gets the width ($91A2), which $939E also reads as the room's X size; for buildings the model's X ($9655), moved towards $80 by the collapse $96AC and set by the rotation $A4FA.
Vertex table: world X middle bytes of vertices 1-3 (part of $0440); room corner 1 gets the room's width at $91A5.
Vertex table: world X middle byte of vertex 4 (part of $0440); room corner 4 gets the width at $91A8.
Vertex table: world X middle bytes of vertices 5-63 (the rest of $0440); room corner 5 gets the width at $91AB, the others come from the building and room loaders.

Vertex table: world height low byte, one per vertex (24-bit with $04C0 and $0780): 0 for building vertices ($95FC, $964C), a template byte for room shapes ($925D). The starfields keep each star's previous screen y here.

Vertex table: world height middle byte of vertex 0 (continued at $04C1-$04C3). A room's corners 0-3 get its height (the ceiling; corners 4-7 are the floor at 0), here by $91B3; for buildings the model's height ($961C, $967E), which the collapse $96AC counts down to 0.
Vertex table: world height middle byte of vertex 1 (part of $04C0); room corner 1, the ceiling height, from $91B6.
Vertex table: world height middle byte of vertex 2 (part of $04C0); room corner 2, the ceiling height, from $91B9.
Vertex table: world height middle bytes of vertices 3-63 (the rest of $04C0); room corner 3 gets the ceiling height from $91BC.
Vertex table: world Y low byte, one per vertex (24-bit with $0540 and $07C0): 0 for rooms and static building vertices ($964F), set by the rotation $A4B2 for a building's turning part.

Vertex table: world Y middle bytes of vertices 0-2 (continued at $0543, $0544, $0547, $057F). Room corner 0 gets the depth ($91C4), which $939E also reads as the room's Y size; building vertices from the model ($965B), moved by the collapse $96AC and the rotation $A539.
Vertex table: world Y middle byte of vertex 3 (part of $0540); room corner 3 gets the depth at $91C7.
Vertex table: world Y middle bytes of vertices 4-6 (part of $0540); room corner 4 gets the depth at $91CA.
Vertex table: world Y middle bytes of vertices 7-62 (part of $0540); room corner 7 gets the depth at $91CD.
Vertex table: world Y middle byte of vertex 63, the last of $0540. Its symbol comes from STA $057F,Y at $9192, Y 12 down to 1, which fills $0580-$058B with the room box's edge starts from $933B.

Edge list, 64 entries: the first vertex of each edge (the second at $05C0). The building loader $9575 unpacks the model's edges (high nibble, or the first of two bytes); the room builder copies the box's 12 edges ($9192) and chains each template shape's vertices ($9275). $96E7 draws edges $71 down to 0.
Edge list: the first vertex of edge 63, the last of $0580. Its symbol comes from STA $05BF,Y at $9198, Y 12 down to 1, which fills $05C0-$05CB with the box's edge ends from $9347.
Edge list, 64 entries: the second vertex of each edge (pair of $0580): the model's low nibble or second byte ($95CB, $95DE), the box's from $9347, the next vertex of a room shape ($927C).
Vertex table: X'/Z mantissa, one per vertex (exponents at $03C0), the perspective x from $A75C ($5E); the clipper $99DD reloads it.
Vertex table: exponent byte of Y'/Z, one per vertex (the mantissas are at $7600), from $61 by $A94D; read by $99DD.

Vertex table: screen x (0-159) of each projected vertex ($A952), a line end for $99DD and the dot of a distant object ($ADD8). The starfields keep each star's current screen x here ($73F5, $AB77), 1 before the first frame ($7304, $AA85).
Vertex table: screen y (0-135) of each projected vertex ($A957). The starfields keep each star's current screen y here ($73F0, $AB72), 1 before the first frame ($7301, $AA82).

Vertex table: clip code of each projected vertex from $A75C ($6E): bit 7 behind the viewer, bit 0 x off screen, bit 1 y off screen, 0 on screen. $99DD drops an edge with both ends behind; $ADCB plots a distant object's dot only when it is 0.
Vertex table: world X high byte (the grid column), one per vertex: the player's $74 for building vertices ($95F2, $963F), 0 in rooms.
Vertex table: world height high byte, one per vertex, always 0: cleared by $B8F6 at every zero-page swap, by the room builder $9162 and by the star setup $72FA; nothing else writes it.
Vertex table: world Y high byte (the grid row), one per vertex: the player's $7A for building vertices ($95F7, $9644), 0 in rooms.

City map, roads along X (east-west, X growing eastwards by the leaflet), first end: 256 bytes, one per square, index Y*16+X. A number p is the centre of square (p AND 15, p/16) on the ground ($A67B), and every square on a road holds the same pair: 15 roads. Read at $8F24 (the player's square, to $757D) and at $8F66, whose operand $8EF1/$8F58 set to each row in view: $8FC3 adds each road to the line lists $7540, $7580/$75C0 that $9054 draws when flying (radius by height from $2A00, none below 2048 units).

City map, roads along X, second end: for each square (Y*16+X) the number of the square at the higher-X end of the X-direction road through it, paired with map_road_x_from ($2C00). Read at $8F2A (the player's square, to $757C, the slot $90A6 tests) and $8F6B (squares in view, passed to $8FC3 in A).

City map, roads along Y (north-south), first end: for each square (Y*16+X) the number of the square at the lower-Y end of the Y-direction road through it, 0 = none; 17 roads, such as $01-$F1 down column 1. Read at $8F30 (the player's square, to $757F) and $8F71 (squares in view; a 0 skips the pair).

City map, roads along Y, second end: the number of the square at the higher-Y end of the Y-direction road through each square, paired with map_road_y_from ($2E00). Read at $8F36 (to $757E, tested at $90B2) and $8F76 (squares in view).

Underground room records, 174 of them (rooms $01-$AE; pointers split at $2300/$23C0, read at $90FA; entries 0 and $AF-$BF point here too, and room 0 means outside). Format, from $90F6-$9287 and $9437: byte 0 = X size in units of 256 (bit 7: a transporter booth, below); byte 1 bits 0-2 = height, bits 3-7 = n; byte 2 = Y size (bit 7 set: on entry start script n through $8A8C, clear: show canned message n through $F7); bytes 3, 4 = two colours (to $C4, $C5, then $A5, $A6: the low nibble of the view's screen matrix and its colour RAM). Then doors of 4 bytes: type, destination room, X, Y (the unit the door is in); type bit 7 = in a wall of constant X, else constant Y; bits 4-6 = the door of the destination room the player comes out of; bits 0-3 = outline, through $932B into $928A (2 plain, 3 triangle, 4/5 arrows, 6 cross, 7 diagonal, 9-15 locked: needs bit 7 of $29C0 of object 8+outline, the key). The list ends in 0, or in $80 for a dark room. A booth adds link pairs (room, door in bits 4-6) after the end: two at bytes 10-13, eight in room $72. Script step: the event-script interpreter, one operation per call, from the main loop $855C and the opening sequence's loops ($7319, $74F2, $AA95). Returns at once while a message is printing ($E6 non-zero), so every script waits for Benson to finish. Otherwise it reads the operation byte at the script pointer ($1F),0 into $E7 (bit 7 inverts a test, bit 6 makes a taken test a call), writes $8D5E + 2 x (op AND $3F) into the pointer of the JMP ($8D5E) at $8ACC and so jumps to that operation's handler. Handlers read their operands through ($1F),Y and finish at $8B92 (move $1F/$20 past the operation) or $8BB2 (move it to a target).
Script dispatch, low byte: the pointer operand of JMP ($8D5E) at $8ACC, rewritten on every step by $8AC2 with $5E + 2 x op, so that the jump reads the handler's address out of the table $8D5E.
Script dispatch, high byte of the same pointer: $8D plus the carry out of the low byte, written by $8AC9 (the table ends at $8DA3, so it is always $8D).

Script op 24, if peek: operands a memory address (low, high) and a value, then the two-byte target. Writes the address into the CMP at $8ADF ($8AE0/$8AE1) and compares the value with the byte found there: the branch is taken when that byte is greater than the value, or, with bit 7 of the op, when it is not. Its one use, at $0E6F, tests $7700 > 0, credits of 1,000,000 or more, before the 999,999-credit ship hire.
Op 24's address, low byte: the operand of CMP $0100 at $8ADF, written from the script by $8AD3.
Op 24's address, high byte, written by $8AD9; the $0100 in the snapshot is only a placeholder.

Script op 10, if random: one operand, then the target. Steps the random generator $ADEF and branches when the operand is below the new random byte $E8, or, with bit 7, when $E8 is at most the operand. The scripts use it inverted with $80, taken for 129 values of 256 ($0A74, $0CD4, $0CDB).

Script op 7, if clock: a number of seconds (low, high), then the target. Reads the seconds clock $E3 (low) and $E4 (high), again if $E3 changed between the reads (the panel interrupt counts it), and branches while the clock is below the number; bit 7 branches once it has reached it. With op 2 it makes the scripts' waits: $0A8F clears the clock and loops on op 7 for two seconds.

Script op 23: one operand, then the target. Branches when the signed byte $BEBD is below the operand minus 128 (it compares $BEBD EOR $80 with the operand, unsigned); bit 7 inverts. No script in this image uses it, and op 22 is the only other code that touches $BEBD.

Script op 34, if craft: one operand, then the target. Branches when $A9, the number of the object the player is riding ($80 on foot, $98E2), equals the operand. Script 0 waits at $09BB for 1, the Dart; script 7 tests 7, the interstellar ship ($1096, $10D3).

Script op 29, no operands, then the target: branches when object $57EE lies in room $57EF ($2940 + object holds the room an object is in, 0 outdoors, $FF while carried). $0E0C: the Antenna (30) in the Communication Room ($10).

Script op 19, no operands, then the target: branches when the player is in room $57EF, compared with the current room $CD (0 outdoors). The briefings run it inverted ($0CF1, $0DC7) to stop when the player walks out.
Script op 18, if flags: a mask, then the target. Branches when any bit of the mask is set in the script flags $BEC0 (bit 7 of the op inverts).

Script op 12, if carried: no operands, then the target. Branches when object $57EE is in the player's carried list $BEB1 ($941A). The Communication Room ($0E0F) and the interstellar ship ($10A4) look for the Antenna and the Novadrive this way.
Script op 9: a machine-code address (low, high), then the target. Calls it through $8C5D and branches when it comes back with the carry clear. No script in this image uses it (see $8C5D).
Script op 6: a grid X and a grid Y, then the target. Branches when the player's square, $74 and $7A, is that one (underground both are 0). No script in this image uses it.

Script op 31, no operands, then the target: branches when variable $57ED equals $B7, the location number of the player's square (Y x 16 + X, 0 outside the city, set at $952B). No script in this image uses it.

Script op 11, if key: a key number, then the target. When the last key $E9, SHIFT and CTRL bits dropped, equals the operand, it forgets the key ($B4B2), calls $B94D (sound 0 on voice 1) and branches; otherwise it goes on. The scripts poll it in a loop against the clock: Y ($19) at $0AB6 (buy, hire) and $10CF (launch).

Script op 26, no operands, then the target: branches when bit 7 of $2B00 + $57ED is set, the building at location $57ED destroyed. The escape at $10E6 sets $57ED to $32 (02-03, the author's advert) and will not leave while it is.

Script op 33: a mask, then the target. Branches when any bit of the mask is set in object $57EE's flags $29C0 (bit 0 sold, 2 starts its script and 3 prints its name when taken ($98B1), 4 cannot be taken, 5 too heavy without the Antigrav, 7 carried). The shops test bit 0 at $1010.

Script test tail, shared by every test: enter at $8B87 when the condition is false, at $8B8A when true, or at $8B8B with the carry clear for true. The carry goes into bit 7 and bit 7 of the op ($E7) inverts it. Not taken: the pointer moves past the two-byte target to the next operation ($8B90). Taken: $8B9E jumps to the target, or calls it when bit 6 of the op is set ($8BA3). $8B92 is also where the other operations end: $1F/$20 += Y + 1, Y being the index of their last operand.

Script op 4, call: a two-byte target. Pushes the address of this operation + 3 on the script stack (low, then high, $8BC9) and jumps. A taken test with bit 6 set enters here too and pushes the same + 3, which is right only for op 4; no script in this image sets bit 6.
Script op 3, jump: loads the script pointer $1F/$20 with the two-byte target. Every taken test ends here.
Script op 5, return: pops the script pointer from the script stack ($8BD2: the high byte, then the low).

Script stack push: stores A at $BEC2 + $E5 and raises the index $E5. The stack holds the return addresses of script calls ($8BA3) and of scripts started as calls by $8A8C; $7203 empties it at start-up.
Script stack pop: lowers $E5 and returns the byte at $BEC2 + $E5 in A.

Script op 32: one mask for object $57EE's flags $29C0. Below $80 it sets the mask's bits; $80 and above it ANDs the flags with the mask, clearing the bits that are 0 in it. Bit 7 (carried) cannot change either way. The shops set $11 at $1039: sold (bit 0) and no longer takeable (bit 4).

Script op 15, set variable: a variable number (low nibble) and a value for $57E0 + n. The scripts use $57EE for an object number, $57EF for a room number and $57ED for a location number (Y x 16 + X). Setting $57ED also writes that location as the word 'XX-YY' at $BEF9-$BEFD (dictionary word $CB, digits by $8C23), which no message in this image prints.

Location digits: writes the two decimal digits of X (0-15), from the BCD table $803A, at $BEF9 + Y and $BEFA + Y and returns with Y + 1. The second character is the whole BCD byte, so 10-15 give $10-$15, which the printer shows in the message font's digits ($90-$95) instead of the figures $00-$09.

Script op 1, print: the message tokens that follow, up to a 0. Points the printer's token read (the operand $8E27/$8E28 of the LDY at $8E26) at this operation, whose first token is one byte on, skips the tokens and starts the printer: $E6 = $FF, token index $DE and character index $DF = 0. The next step then waits until the message has been shown.
Script op 2, clock reset: zeroes the seconds clock $E3-$E4, the start of every timed wait (op 7).
Script op 8: calls the machine code at the two-byte address that follows ($8C5D), then goes on. No script in this image uses it.

Calls the machine code whose address (low, high) follows in the script, by writing it into the JSR at $8C69. That JSR comes back to $8C6C, op 13's handler, so a routine ending in a plain RTS would go on to run op 13 on the script's next bytes; only one that drops its own return address would return cleanly. Ops 8 and 9, its only callers, are unused in this image.
The JSR that ops 8 and 9 aim, by rewriting its operand $8C6A/$8C6B; in the snapshot it points at itself.
Low byte of the machine-code address that ops 8 and 9 call, written by $8C60.
High byte of the machine-code address that ops 8 and 9 call, written by $8C66.

Script op 13, set counter: a counter number n (low nibble) and four BCD bytes, least significant first, stored at $76E3 + 4n down to $76E0 + 4n: a counter is big-endian in memory. It shares op 14's loop, first turning the ADC $76E3,X at $8C89 into BIT $76E3 so that the loop stores instead of adding. The intro sets counter 8, the credits, to 9000 ($710C); the shops set counter 9, the reward on offer.

Script op 14, add to counter: counter n and four BCD bytes, least significant first, added in decimal mode; the carry out of the top byte is lost. Puts the ADC back at $8C89. There is no subtraction: $0A29 adds 99995000 to take 5000 credits for the Dart, $0E90 adds 99000001 to take 999999 for the Hertz ship.
Opcode of the counter loop's ADC $76E3,X: op 13 writes $2C (BIT $76E3, so the loop stores the script's bytes) and op 14 writes back $7D (ADC).
Script op 21, sum counters: three counter numbers a, b, c (low nibbles): counter c = counter a + counter b in BCD, the carry out lost. Used once, at $1041: credits (8) = reward (9) + credits (8).
Script op 30, copy variable: one byte, the destination in the high nibble and the source in the low: $57E0 + high = $57E0 + low. $104C-$105B save and restore $57EE/$57EF in $57E8/$57E9 this way.

Script op 16, set flags: ORs its operand into the script flags $BEC0, which ops 17 and 18 clear and test. The scripts use bit 0 for a yes answer ($0AC2), 1 for opposition sites destroyed ($11F5), 2 for the ship despatched ($0EBE), 3 for the author's advert destroyed ($0B6B) and 5 for the brother-in-law offended ($0A67).
Script op 17, clear flags: clears the bits of its operand in $BEC0. Scripts started as calls end with it on bit 6 ($40), the busy bit that $8A8C sets and checks before it starts another.

Script op 25, poke: an address (low, high) and a value, stored there by the STA at $8D1C, whose operand ($8D1D/$8D1E) it rewrites. The scripts poke the printer's timers $E0/$E1, SID voices 1 and 2 ($D404, $D40B), $7000, $296E and $BEF8, $BEFE, $BEFF.
Op 25's address, low byte: the operand of STA $0100 at $8D1C, written by $8D10.
Op 25's address, high byte, written by $8D16; the snapshot's $0100 is only a placeholder.

Script op 20, message: a canned message number (0-63); with bit 7 set the number is read from variable $57E0 + (low nibble). Starts it through $8DAA. A number above 63 is not checked and would read past the 64-entry pointer tables.

Script op 27, random message: a mask and a base; starts canned message (random AND mask) + base ($ADEF, then $8DAA). Used once, at $08B7: one of messages 60-63 after the crash (WHERE AM I, YOU CRASHED, GOOD LANDING!, OUCH!). A sum of 0 would fall into op 28 instead and print nothing.
Script op 28, clear key: forgets the last key ($B4B2 stores $04 in $E9), so that a following key test needs a fresh press; used before the yes/no questions ($0AAB, $0E4C, $10B9).
Script op 22: adds its signed operand to $BEBD, saturating at -128 ($80) and +127 ($7F) instead of wrapping. No script in this image uses it, nor op 23, the only other code that touches $BEBD.
A spare $00 byte between op 22's handler and the handler table: the dispatch indexes from $8D5E, and no instruction reads it.

Script handlers: 35 addresses indexed by operation number (op AND $3F), read by the JMP ($8D5E) at $8ACC. Entry 0 is $0000 and no script uses op 0. 1 print $8C36, 2 clock reset $8C4E, 3 jump $8BB2, 4 call $8BA3, 5 return $8BBE, 6 if square $8B47, 7 if clock $8AF0, 8 call code $8C57, 9 if code $8B41, 10 if random $8AE5, 11 if key $8B60, 12 if carried $8B37, 13 set counter $8C6C, 14 add to counter $8C73, 15 set variable $8BF5, 16 set flags $8CF3, 17 clear flags $8CFF, 18 if flags $8B2D, 19 if player in room $8B24, 20 message $8D22, 21 sum counters $8C98, 22 add to $BEBD $8D46, 23 if $BEBD below $8B03, 24 if peek $8AD0, 25 poke $8D0D, 26 if destroyed $8B72, 27 random message $8D34, 28 clear key $8D40, 29 if object in room $8B17, 30 copy variable $8CDB, 31 if at location $8B57, 32 object flags $8BDB, 33 if object flags $8B7C, 34 if craft $8B0E.
